newsitem.title: UK: American Phoenix acquires Lloyd's broker LPF.
newsitem.headline: American Phoenix acquires Lloyd's broker LPF.

text.p: U.S. insurance broker American Phoenix Corporation has acquired a majority shareholding in Lloyd's of London insurance broker Lees Preston Fairy (LPF), according to a statement on Tuesday.

"Lees Preston Fairy has received an approach from American Phoenix Corporation of Hartford, Connecticut, to acquire a majority shareholding in the company. The board consider this to be an exciting development for the long term future and growth of the company, in line with their current strategy of seeking new business opportunities," the statement said.

The acquisition, for an undisclosed sum, represents the first time American Phoenix has expanded outside the U.S., although its parent company Phoenix Home Life Mutual Insurance Company opened a representative office in London last week in response to growing global demand for reinsurance services and products.

American Phoenix is the fifteenth largest insurance broker in the U.S., and the largest without an overseas connection, with 585 staff and producing $63.8 million in revenue. Its parent, Phoenix Home Life Mutual of New York, reported a turnover of more than $2.3 billion in 1995 and total assets of $13 billion.

LPF is a privately-owned company formed in 1989 specialising in insurance and reinsurance in lines such as marine and bankers' blanket bonds. It has an annual turnover of around 1.O million stg, 12 brokers and 20 staff.

The move is the latest in the spate of consolidation seeping through the international broking market among the low-to-middle sized firms as well as the 'big six' market leaders. Last week U.S. giant Aon scooped up rival Alexander & Alexander for $1.23 billion, and on Monday London market broker Lloyd Thompson merged with Jardine Insurance Brokers.
"In the current climate of consolidation in the insurance broking market, LPF's pedigree as a niche broker will continue to be supported," an LPF spokesman said.
